headline: The agriculture minister forecast a 2026 grape crop of about 3.85 million tonnes, up from about 2.5 million in 2025.
body: Speaking at a harvest event in Kalecik, Ankara, İbrahim Yumaklı called 2026 the wettest year in 66 years. TÜİK's first crop estimate in May had already pointed to a 53% rise in grape production.
why: After the poor 2025 crop, a large harvest should ease grape supply and prices for wineries that buy fruit. Most of the crop is table and drying grapes, so the effect on wine grapes specifically is not stated.
